A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CodeBrain research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the revised title, formatting, and section organization.

before.justification: v2 reports original downstream classification results, tokenizer and backbone ablations, interpretability analyses, robustness experiments, and scaling studies.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, codebook ablations, perturbation tests, computational measurements, and low-resource evaluations.

M1.justification: The two-stage tokenizer/EEGSSM procedure, objectives, dual codebooks, contrastive learning, SGConv, sliding-window attention, and gating remain unchanged. v3 specifies the positional convolution as following ACPE, but this expands implementation documentation without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: The pretraining corpus and eight tasks across ten datasets remain, but tested input conditions expand substantially. v3 adds selective frequency-band removal, anatomically structured channel loss, and non-stationary baseline drift on SEED-V and ISRUC_S3, extending coverage beyond v2's random channel-dropout scenarios.

E2.justification: v3 adds EEGNet, EEGConformer, ContraWR, and ST-Transformer to the actual comparisons across all ten datasets (Table 2 and Appendix I). v2 evaluated five EFMs and explicitly excluded traditional supervised comparators. v3 also adds an efficiency comparison against the five EFMs in Table 22.

E3.justification: v3 adds frozen-backbone linear probing, 10% labeled-data fine-tuning, codebook masking, and controlled perturbation protocols. The class-specific-token threshold is corrected to include equality. CHB-MIT subject allocations also change from 1-19/20-21/22-23 to 1-20 with exclusions/21-22/23-24 in the dataset appendix; the PDFs do not establish whether those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test tokenizer removal and masking frequently activated codes (B.4), SGConv decay sensitivity and frequency-band dependence (K.5-K.6), regional dropout and baseline drift (M.2-M.3), computational scaling (N.3), and additional low-resource transfer settings (O). These substantially extend the questions investigated beyond v2's retained ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and report means and standard deviations. The added result rows follow this existing practice; no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Existing main-table CodeBrain scores remain unchanged, but substantial baseline, ablation, robustness, probing, and compute results are added. On BCIC 2020-T3, the highest baseline Kappa changes from CBraMod's 0.4216 to newly included EEGConformer's 0.4488, while CodeBrain remains at 0.5127. New ISRUC_S3 ablations report Kappa 0.7503 for raw reconstruction and 0.7426 for masked codebooks.

T1.justification: The class-specific-token definition changes from Dominance(c) > 1 to Dominance(c) >= 1 (v2 A.3; v3 B.3), correcting an impossible criterion. The state-space and rate-distortion propositions and derivations are otherwise retained; the new independence remark supplies interpretation rather than a revised proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion narrow interpretability to representation-level structure, and the contribution statement now says some tokens correspond to physiological patterns. The central method, generalization, robustness, and scalability claims otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly distinguishes representation-level from decision-level interpretability and states the scalp-EEG applicability boundary (Appendix P). Appendix D reinterprets independence in latent semantic terms despite Fourier coupling. The SWA discussion is corrected to acknowledge that larger windows do not consistently help, and the new analyses add substantial physiological, robustness, and deployment interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 promises a future code and weight release; v3 states they are available and supplies repository access information. v3 also documents random codebook initialization with L2 normalization, five warm-up steps, contrastive temperature 0.5, the ACPE positional convolution, token-selection details, and GPU counts and training durations. These are newly reported disclosures, not established implementation changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Uni-NTFM, ECHO, XaiGuiFormer, EEGConformer, and ContraWR, and explicitly attributes the positional convolution to CBraMod's ACPE. Related work revises the characterization of later tokenizers from uniformly using mixed-domain codebooks to frequency-dominant approaches. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Related work moves from main Section 2 to Appendix A, and additional results precede hyperparameter details. v3 adds an appendix contents page and reporting statements, revises the title and terminology, and locally rewrites interpretability and SWA explanations. Most existing methodological and experimental prose is retained.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands comparison and low-resource tables, adds nine analysis tables, and changes the document layout and table styling. Figures 1 and 4 are revised. Figure 3 replaces a duplicated FACED panel with SEED-V scaling results already present in v2's appendix; this corrects their display rather than introducing new results. Most appendix figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves scrutiny of the retained method through codebook-removal tests, broader comparisons, and structured failure-condition analyses. Reproducibility disclosures, interpretability qualifications, and the Figure 3 and token-threshold corrections also help. The net gain is limited by reporting inconsistencies: Section 3.3 still identifies CBraMod as the strongest BCIC Kappa baseline despite Table 2, and the new main-text description calls the 146.75M model 12-layer while the retained scaling tables specify 24 layers.
